html:
The First Anglo-Afghan War was the British invasion of Afghanistan from 1839 to 1842, which ended in the destruction of a British and Indian army on the retreat from Kabul.

In the Great Game with Russia, the East India Company feared the emir Dost Mohammad Khan and sent an army to put the old king Shah Shuja on the throne. It took Kabul easily in 1839. But Afghans rose against the occupiers, and in late 1841 the British envoy was killed.

In January 1842 the garrison, about 4,500 soldiers and some 12,000 camp followers, set out in winter through the passes toward Jalalabad. Almost all were killed, captured or died of cold. A British army of retribution burned part of Kabul later that year, then left, and Dost Mohammad returned to rule. Britain tried again in 1878, and lost a brigade at Maiwand.
sum: The First Anglo-Afghan War was the British invasion of Afghanistan from 1839 to 1842, which ended in the destruction of a British and Indian army on the retreat from Kabul.
